channel.title: Comments on: Drop-shadows Don’t Fill Shopping Carts
channel.description: Instant Usability & Web Standards — static archive

item.title: By: Daniel Szuc
item.dc:creator: Daniel Szuc
item.description: We see a lot of bad copy on web sites in Asia, basically marketing materials just uploaded directly onto the web channel without any thought for the overall “conversation” the user wants to have with the company. Web content is seen as the “odd man out” for web site developments. What web sites have you seen where care is taken in writing good copy? I quite like the tone and style used on the Google site when presenting their product information. Of course Apple :) Others?

item.title: By: Eric Meyer
item.dc:creator: Eric Meyer
item.description: We’re definitely serious about doing AEA in Europe, though we can’t say when and where (because we don’t yet know ourselves). My fervent hope is that we’ll be in Europe in 2008!

item.title: By: Lars Jacobsen
item.dc:creator: Lars Jacobsen
item.description:
Interesting – especially when you combine it with the eye-tracking results (http://www.useit.com/alertbox/banner-blindness.html) that shows the people fixate naturally on text.

Another thing – to often webshops just copy the text from the products page of the manufacturer, and often without translating it. That probably hurts just as much as choosing the wrong colour on the check-out cart :-)
